text:
sarah: Heads-up — noticed unusual KV residency growth on prod GPU nodes since the kernel-selection change yesterday. One tenant is holding ~40% more pages than expected.
raj: saw that in perf dash too. spikes line up with long-context traffic from that tenant (avg seq_len 6k). Paging rate up ~3x.
megan: any obvious eviction pressure? I checked per-tenant watermarks and it looks like our global eviction sweep is treating that tenant as low priority.
kevin: yeah, kernel change bumped batch packing heuristics which increased prefix reuse but also increased long-lived KV allocations for some sessions. We probably widened the active KV segment sizes.
sarah: repro steps i ran:
```
# quick repro on staging
ab-run --profile --seq 6k --tenants heavy-1 --duration 20m
kubectl logs runtime-0 | grep KV_PAGE_WALK | tail -n 50
```
output shows repeated pagewalks and >200MB persistent per-session KV.
raj: interesting — paging seems to happen without eviction falling back. I think the eviction scanner only looks at LRU timestamps and misses pages pinned by recent long contexts.
megan: could be fragmentation + pinned slices. fragmentation report from the profiler:
- total pages: 1.9M
- free contig run < 16 pages: 62%
- avg slice size for tenant heavy-1: 18 pages
kevin: that matches my threads: we tolerate many small allocations and compaction hasn't run because compaction threshold is >1k freed pages.
sarah: immediate mitigation idea: per-tenant soft quotas + early compaction trigger if a tenant's resident pages exceed 2x baseline for 5m. That would reclaim fragmented runs and reduce noisy neighbor impact.
raj: we should also try weighted eviction: score = age * tenant_weight / slice_size. Increase score for tenants above soft-quota.
megan: agreed. We can A/B test weighted eviction on a few GPUs. Question: will it interact badly with KV cache reuse for long-context sessions? Could evict pages that are needed soon.
kevin: to avoid harming short-term reuse, add a 'recently-accessed' grace window: pages touched within last X seconds get a penalty to eviction score.
sarah: proposed experiment plan:
1) rollout weighted-evict (tenant_weight) to 10% of rings, target tenants heavy-1 + heavy-2
2) enable early compaction at lower threshold on those rings
3) monitor per-tenant P95 latency, pagewalks/sec, eviction_count, memory-residency
4) rollback if per-tenant P95 increases >5% or model failures increase
raj: metrics to track (prom names):
- runtime_kv_pagewalk_total
- runtime_kv_eviction_count{tenant}
- runtime_kv_resident_pages{tenant}
- runtime_infer_p95_ms{tenant}
megan: i'll add dashboards and a pager rule for sudden resident_pages growth.
kevin: small perf-regression note: after enabling weighted-evict locally i saw a 1.2% tail latency bump for short chat flows — probably due to extra eviction CPU overhead. We need to micro-opt the scoring code (use integer ops, avoid locks).
sarah: action items:
- kevin: implement tenant_weight config + integer scoring and a grace-window flag (owner: kevin, ETA: 2d)
- megan: dashboards + alert (owner: megan, ETA: EOD)
- raj: pick 10% rings and tell infra to route (owner: raj, ETA: tomorrow morning)
- sarah: run baseline job and collect perf snapshot (owner: sarah, ETA: today)

kevin: i'll also add an opt-in that restricts compaction to background threads when GPU utilization > 80% so we don't thrash.
megan: noted. also adding a short lockdown policy: if total resident pages on a node jumps > 20% in 10m, autoscale down noisy tenant or throttle requests.
sarah: final note: log schema to add `kv_eviction_reason` and `tenant_quota_exceeded` tag so we can correlate: will file a small PR.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime:v2026-03-19-alpha to 10% rings (note: weighted-evict feature flag disabled by default)
raj: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after 24h of experiment data. :thumbsup:
